CRYPTO NEWS — August 13, 2026

Sideways grind continues. Bitcoin shrugged off a match-forecast CPI report this morning, staying locked in its narrow $63.3k-$64.3k range with zero directional impulse. Fear gauge ticked up marginally to 29, confirming traders remain cautious with dry powder sitting heavy at $255B in stables. Alts underperforming as expected—only Solana showing resilience with weekly gains. Funding rates stay flat, leverage suppressed, and the market looks primed to break either way without conviction steering it there. Let's see what moves the needle.

TODAY'S HIGHLIGHTS

SEC Greenlights Crypto Startup Exemption Rule (Friday Vote)
The SEC scheduled an open meeting for August 14 to consider new rules enabling crypto projects to raise capital without registering securities, with SEC Chair Paul Atkins spearheading a "Regulation Crypto Assets" framework that proposes a startup exemption granting developers up to four years of regulatory runway to achieve network decentralization. The proposed rule provides an escape hatch from SEC jurisdiction once project founders cease active management of their protocols. TD Cowen analyst Jaret Seiberg identified the proposal as the first in a series of rulemakings intended to establish durable regulatory certainty for digital assets. What it means: Regulatory certainty is cheap marketing right now. If passed, this becomes a genuine catalyst for early-stage tokens and projects seeking to launch defensibly. Mark Friday as a watch date—if this sails through, expect brief outperformance in smaller-cap tokens seeking legit runway. Otherwise it's noise.

Russia Legalizes Retail Bitcoin & Ether Trading (First Time)
The Bank of Russia published a draft directive on August 11 establishing its first framework to allow non-qualified retail investors to trade digital assets through licensed brokers and exchanges, capping non-qualified investor purchases at 300,000 rubles per year, and regulators approved only three digital assets for public exchange trading: Bitcoin, Ether and Tether's USDT. What it means: Russia was a dead zone for legit retail access. This regulatory thaw opens $150B+ in retail capital in theory, but the annual cap ($3.6k per person) kills the narrative fast. Still, it's directional proof that macro regulators are shifting permissive. No direct price impact here, but it threads the needle toward bigger institutional flows later.

Solana Momentum Builds: Jupiter Upgrade & Ecosystem Growth
Jupiter launched Lend v2 on August 10 with a novel "Smart Debt" feature that allows borrowed assets to simultaneously function as decentralized exchange (DEX) liquidity, earning trading fees that can offset borrowing costs, merging lending and liquidity provision to maximize capital efficiency on the network. Solana's network stablecoin value hit $16.7B, signaling strong adoption for payments and transfers. What it means: SOL is the altcoin doing work—not just price, but actual ecosystem depth. Jupiter's upgrade is capital-efficient and tangible; stablecoin growth on-chain suggests real traction, not speculation. SOL's +3.3% weekly performance and lower funding rates align with this. Traders: SOL's still the altcoin to monitor if risk appetite returns.

WATCH LIST

24–48h pivots: Bitcoin's close above $64,329 (24h high) triggers momentum logic and retest of resistance; break below $63,267 (24h low) extends weekly downtrend and risks liquidation cascades. Solana's structural strength (ecosystem, funding, weekly momentum) makes it a proxy bet on broad altcoin reversal—watch if it holds $75–76 support. SEC's August 14 vote Friday is a macro pin event; approval could spark a brief rotation into smaller-cap layer-1s and dev-friendly tokens. Ethereum's funding remains elevated at 0.0065%; watch for a de-leverage flush if BTC rolls over. Stablecoin liquidity floor remains robust—no capitulation signal yet. Net: Range-bound but tight. Either direction breaks cleanly if one catalyst sticks.

See you tomorrow — stay sharp.
